title: Analysts Flag Nine Sensex Stocks With Up to 43% Upside as Market Correction Deepens
excerpt: Amid foreign capital outflows and elevated oil prices driven by the US-Iran conflict, market strategists see deep value forming in blue-chip Indian stocks across IT, banking, defence and consumer sectors.
body:
• Market strategist Rahul Ghose identifies 10 high-conviction stocks with 12-month upside ranging from 17% to 43%, led by Dixon Technologies and Infosys
  • Indian markets have been pressured by foreign capital outflows, elevated crude prices and rupee weakness tied to the US-Iran conflict
  • Analysts expect FY27 earnings growth of 13–15% and note that domestic institutional investors are providing a strong floor
  • Key catalysts include the 8th Pay Commission, income tax relief, GST rationalization and potential de-escalation in West Asia

Indian equity markets have endured months of selling pressure as the US-Iran war keeps crude oil elevated and foreign institutional investors pull capital. But a growing cohort of market strategists argues the correction has pushed several Sensex heavyweights into compelling risk-reward territory.

Rahul Ghose, founder and CEO of Octanom Tech and Hedged.in, told Mint that domestic institutional investors have "decisively stepped up, providing a strong floor." He expects earnings growth to revert to a 13–15% trend in FY27, supported by monetary easing that could drive GDP growth of around 7.5%.

The Top Picks

Dixon Technologies leads the list with a 43% upside target of ₹15,000, driven by a 67.8% year-over-year profit jump in Q3 FY26 and its entry into Apple's iPhone supply chain. The stock has corrected over 42% from its 52-week high.

Infosys, trading near its 52-week low at around ₹1,300, carries a target of ₹1,800 — a 41% upside. Ghose pointed to improving deal flow, GenAI projects scaling from proof-of-concept to production, and a healthy dividend payout of 65.9% with three-year ROE of 30.7%.

Eternal (formerly Zomato) has a ₹310 target implying 31% upside, with Blinkit now the primary growth engine. Sun Pharmaceutical Industries carries a ₹2,100 target (27% upside) as its US specialty dermatology portfolio begins delivering meaningful revenue.

Defence, Banking and Infrastructure

Larsen & Toubro's record order book of ₹5.79 lakh crore — a 22% increase — supports a ₹4,900 target (24% upside). Its defence division is growing at over 40% annually.

"History suggests all three tend to happen faster than the market fears. Historical data from the 1990 Gulf War, 2003 Iraq War, and 2023 Israel-Hamas conflict consistently show that the Sensex delivers strong double-digit returns within 12 months."

— Rahul Ghose, Founder and CEO, Hedged.in

Hindustan Aeronautics, debt-free with strong cash flows, has a ₹5,000 target (22% upside) after correcting sharply from ₹5,165. ICICI Bank, with a gross NPA of just 1.53% and net NPA of 0.37%, carries a consensus target of ₹1,650 (22% upside).

SBI Life Insurance (₹2,300 target, 20% upside) benefits from SBI's unmatched distribution network and India's low insurance penetration. Bharti Airtel, with over 650 million customers, has a ₹2,200 target (18% upside) as 5G monetization begins. Titan rounds out the list with a ₹5,200 target (17% upside) after revenue rose 42% year-over-year in Q3 FY26.

Risks Remain but Catalysts Are Building

The near-term outlook hinges on crude oil prices. Analysts warn that if prices remain elevated for more than two to three months, India's inflation could rise by 55–60 basis points and GDP growth may drop to around 6%.

For foreign capital to return aggressively, markets need a definitive de-escalation in West Asia, cooling crude prices, and rupee stabilization. But multiple domestic catalysts are building: the 8th Pay Commission, income tax relief and GST rationalization are expected to underpin consumption demand through the year.

HSBC Global Research has maintained its Sensex end-2026 target at 94,000, implying over 10% upside, while forecasting large-cap earnings growth of 14% in FY27.

What to Watch

Investors should monitor Q1 FY27 results closely. Motilal Oswal recently upgraded Bajaj Finserv to a Buy with a ₹2,490 target after the company posted 12% profit growth in Q1. Broader sectoral indicators — particularly FMCG, banking and financial services — have shown a positive bias, suggesting the market correction may be nearing an inflection point for patient, fundamentals-driven investors.
